#| code-fold: show

`r if (py$plain_loss > 0.9 * py$chance_loss) "No" else "Yes"`.
Its training loss after 5 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$plain_loss)`,
against $\log 10 \approx `r sprintf("%.3f", py$chance_loss)`$ for probabilities of $\frac{1}{10}$.
It classifies `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$plain_acc)`% of the test images correctly.
The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) that reaches its first layer has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_grad)`.
The last block's output has standard deviation `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_std)`.
`r if (py$plain_grad < 1e-4) "So the gradient vanishes before it reaches the first layer, as in the [backpropagation chapter](backpropagation.qmd#def-vanishing-gradient)." else ""`
